outcome_detail: Active in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Mississippi (Schmidt v. Rankin County, Mississippi, 3:25-cv-00909, filed November 25, 2025). Rankin County moved in December 2025 to dismiss official-capacity and punitive-damages claims; briefing on that motion ran through early March 2026 and pre-discovery disclosures were exchanged in February 2026. No settlement or judgment reported as of July 2026.
criminal_detail: Former deputies Christian Dedmon, Hunter Elward and Daniel Opdyke pleaded guilty in 2023 to federal civil rights crimes and related state charges as members of the Rankin County 'Goon Squad'; Dedmon's federal plea covered the December 2022 assault on Alan Schmidt as well as the January 2023 torture of Michael Jenkins and Eddie Parker. In March 2024 Dedmon was sentenced to 40 years in federal prison, Elward to about 20 years and Opdyke to about 17.5 years; Elward and Opdyke admitted failing to intervene in the Schmidt assault.
description: Alan Schmidt, identified in reporting as a victim of Rankin County's 'Goon Squad' deputies, filed a federal civil rights lawsuit on November 25, 2025 against Rankin County and former deputies Christian Dedmon, Hunter Elward and Daniel Opdyke. The suit alleges that during a December 2022 stop, deputies beat Schmidt while he was handcuffed, pressed his arm into an anthill, fired a gun near his head, shocked him with a Taser, and that Dedmon exposed himself and attempted to rub his genitals in Schmidt's face. Dedmon pleaded guilty to federal civil rights charges covering the Schmidt assault and was sentenced to 40 years in prison, while Elward and Opdyke pleaded guilty to related charges including failing to stop the beating. According to the complaint, the sheriff's department was responsible for a broader pattern of misconduct by deputies and jail guards. The case remains active in the Southern District of Mississippi.
notes: Outside strict police-department definition (sheriff). Same scandal as the Michael Jenkins/Eddie Parker 'Goon Squad' torture litigation, which settled for $2.5 million in May 2025 and is a separate lawsuit (not part of this record). Plaintiff is the victim and is publicly named in coverage as an adult male plaintiff suing in his own name.
